newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil panel delays until Tuesday vote on oil bill.
newsitem.headline: Brazil panel delays until Tuesday vote on oil bill.

text.p: A committee in Brazil's Chamber of Deputies delayed until next Tuesday a vote on a bill that would open up the country's petroleum industry to private competition, an official said.

Deputy Alberto Goldman, president of the panel, decided to delay the vote after several members asked for more time to study the latest changes to the bill. The final draft of the bill was due to be put to a vote in a committee in the Chamber of Deputies later today.
Deputy Eliseu Resende, who is the author of the bill, read out a list of alterations to his text which he says did not alter overall aspects of the legislation.
"The philosophy remains the same," Resende said.

Among the changes included by Resende are a clause allowing state-owned Petrobras and private companies to sell naphtha, a petroleum product used to produce petrochemicals, directly to petrochemical consumers. The bill also permits the direct sale of fuel oil to thermoelectric power plants.
A previous version of the bill had stipulated that such sales had to be via state level distributors.

The bill aims to regulate the opening up of Brazil's oil and natural gas sectors, which was approved in theory by Congress in 1995. It would allow private companies to compete or form partnerships with Petrobras and create a regulator to oversee the sector.
If approved by the panel, the bill moves on to the floor of the Chamber of Deputies. It also has to be approved by the Senate.
